entries.appliesTo: persons distributing deceptive and fraudulent synthetic media within 90 days before a Vermont election

dutySources.disclosure-ui: § 2032(a) — 'unless the person includes a disclosure in the synthetic media stating: "This media has been manipulated or generated by digital technology and depicts speech or conduct that did not occur."'

sources.disclosure: § 2032(a) — 'A person shall not, within 90 days before an election in Vermont, publish, communicate, or otherwise distribute synthetic media that the person knows is deceptive and fraudulent synthetic media unless the person includes a disclosure in the synthetic media'
sources.scope: § 2032(a) — 'publish, communicate, or otherwise distribute synthetic media'
sources.windowDays: § 2032(a) — 'within 90 days before an election in Vermont'
sources.penaltyMax: § 2033(a)(3) — 'the person commits the violation with the intent to cause violence or bodily harm and the person commits the violation within five years after one or more prior violations under this section, in which case the fine shall be not more than $15,000.00'
sources.penaltyUnit: § 2033(a)(2) — 'the person commits the violation within five years after one or more prior violations under this section'
sources.enforcer: § 2041 — 'a State's Attorney or the Attorney General may institute any appropriate action, injunction, or other proceeding to prevent, restrain, correct, or abate any violation of this chapter'; § 2033(b) — 'A candidate whose appearance, speech, conduct, or environment is misrepresented … may seek injunctive or other equitable relief'

flags: Category ambiguity: the duty binds 'a person' generally (campaigns, individuals, businesses alike), not businesses specifically; coded company because the regime is a compliance/labeling duty rather than a flat conduct ban, but 'criminal' is arguable — § 2042(a)(3) notice states 'a knowing and intentional violation of this chapter is subject to criminal prosecution'.

Fine tier structure (rule 11): $1,000 base (§ 2033(a)); $5,000 with intent to cause violence or bodily harm (§ 2033(a)(1)); $10,000 for repeat violation within five years (§ 2033(a)(2)); $15,000 for both (§ 2033(a)(3)). No imprisonment terms stated.

Knowledge scienter: disclosure duty applies only to synthetic media 'that the person knows is deceptive and fraudulent synthetic media' (§ 2032(a)); penalties require 'knowingly and intentionally' (§ 2033(a)).

Format specifications for the disclosure: readable text for full duration of video (§ 2032(a)(1)); spoken disclosure at beginning, end, and at intervals of not greater than two minutes for audio over two minutes (§ 2032(a)(2)) — no finer-grained param exists in the election-disclosure vocabulary than disclosure=required.

Exemptions (§ 2032(b)): bona fide newscasts/news coverage with authenticity acknowledgment; paid broadcasts and federally mandated candidate ads; newspapers/periodicals with an accuracy statement; satire or parody; telecommunications/information service providers and interactive computer service providers (47 U.S.C. §§ 153, 230) for content provided by another person.

Separate $5,000 fine for destroying/concealing/falsifying documentary material to evade a civil investigation (§ 2042(b)(2)) — investigation-obstruction penalty, not part of the disclosure regime's penaltyMax.

Sec. 2 (§§ 2041–2042) grants AG/State's Attorney civil investigation powers (document demands, testimony under oath, Superior Court enforcement) chapter-wide; no additional company duty coded from it.
